meta.note: SYNTHETIC triage-scenario dataset for the Phase-49 triage console (blueprint §14 embryo). Curated deterministically from the SYNTHETIC Phase-48 probe history (data/probe-history) — every institution, customer, figure, and panel is invented; no real customer or transaction data. The synthetic-novel stratum quotes committed corpus indicators from US FEDERAL sources only (public domain, 17 U.S.C. §105). Historical dispositions are facts about DECISIONS, never labels of correctness. Regenerate: python3 scripts/curate_triage_scenarios.py

activity: Cash deposits $7,400 / $7,900 / $7,650 across six days — each BELOW the rule's $8,000 floor.
Same weekly rhythm as classic structuring, shifted down one band.
No alert fired; the pattern is invisible to TM-101 as tuned.
P-BT-101.kyc_note: Declared occupation: café owner; expected cash volume declared LOW at onboarding.

activity: Incoming wire $26,000; $22,100 (85%) transferred out 60 hours later.
Misses TM-102 on both arms: under the 90% ratio and outside the 48-hour window.
One earlier near-identical cycle 5 weeks ago. No alert fired.
P-BT-102.kyc_note: No declared source-of-funds note for either incoming wire.

activity: Remittances through two different MSB counterparties to the same beneficiary country: $2,950 + $2,900 + $2,700 in 30 days.
Aggregate $8,550 — UNDER the rule's $9,000 aggregate trigger.
Beneficiary name identical across all three; no alert fired.
P-BT-112.kyc_note: Profile records family in the destination country (a documented connection).

activity: Nine cash deposits in 21 days, every one between $9,300 and $9,900, at three branches.
Each deposit followed within a day by an outbound transfer to the same external account.
Customer asked at the counter about 'the reporting limit' on two occasions (teller notes on file).
P-CT-01.kyc_note: Declared occupation: unemployed. No declared source of funds.

activity: Transaction count 8× the trailing weekly average in the last 7 days.
The spike is the bureau's quarter-end payroll run; identical spikes every quarter-end in history.
Every outbound credit matches a named employee of a documented client company.
P-CT-02.customer: Business account — payroll services bureau, 9-year tenure. SYNTHETIC.
P-CT-02.kyc_note: Client roster and service agreement on file; the velocity rule has no calendar awareness.

activity: Monthly pension credits, utility debits, one annual travel booking.
No cash activity in 5 years.
P-CT-03.customer: Personal account, 31-year tenure, customer age 74. SYNTHETIC.
P-CT-03.kyc_note: KYC current; nothing out of pattern.

activity: Cash deposits at branches in five cities within 10 days, $4,000–7,000 each.
Aggregate $28,500 wired out in one transfer to a money services business in another region.
Branch slips name three different depositors, none the account holder.
P-CT-04.customer: Personal account opened 4 months ago. SYNTHETIC.
P-CT-04.kyc_note: Declared occupation: retail clerk; declared income inconsistent with deposit volume.

activity: Cash deposits $8,400 / $9,100 / $8,950 on three days within one week — each inside the $8,000–9,999 band.
Pattern recurs monthly; this is the NINTH alert on this account for the same behaviour.
All eight prior alerts dismissed (rationale on file each time: 'known cash-intensive side business').
No CTR has ever been triggered; declared occupation: rideshare driver.
P-HF-101.kyc_note: Profile lists a part-time cash side business (unregistered); expected cash volume field BLANK at onboarding.

activity: Incoming e-transfer $21,500, then $19,800 wired out 36 hours later (92% pass-through).
Second cycle three weeks later: $24,000 in, $22,300 out within 40 hours.
Residual balance after each cycle under $2,000. THIRD alert on this account this year; both priors dismissed ('expected property-deal flows').
P-HF-102.kyc_note: Customer note from a prior review mentions 'acting for a relative buying property'; no documentation on file.

activity: Outbound wire $14,200 to a jurisdiction on the institution's high-risk country list.
Customer profile records no business, family, or travel connection to the destination.
Wire memo field: 'family support'. No prior wires to this corridor in account history.
Account otherwise in pattern: salary credits, rent, card spend.
P-HF-104.customer: Personal account, 6-year tenure, salaried profile. SYNTHETIC.
P-HF-104.kyc_note: KYC current (refreshed 14 months ago); occupation: logistics coordinator; no documented overseas ties.

activity: Monthly cash deposits at 240% and 265% of the onboarding-declared expected volume, two consecutive months.
No change filed to the declared nature of business.
Card-settlement credits flat over the same period (sales mix unchanged on the acquiring side).
P-HF-106.customer: Business account — convenience store, 7-year tenure. SYNTHETIC.
P-HF-106.kyc_note: Onboarding profile dated; last KYC refresh 4 years ago. A refresh request is the obvious next step — history shows the review PAUSED for exactly that.

activity: Cash deposits at branches in four cities across two provinces within 12 days ($3,000–6,500 each).
Aggregate $23,800 consolidated, then a single wire out from a fifth city two days later.
Depositor descriptions on branch slips do not consistently match the account holder.
P-HF-109.customer: Personal account opened 11 months ago. SYNTHETIC.
P-HF-109.kyc_note: Declared occupation: student. No employment income credits in account history.

activity: Three incoming wires in 60 days with originator name fields truncated or filled with 'XXX'.
Originating institutions in two different correspondent corridors.
Funds applied to supplier payments consistent with the declared business line.
P-HF-110.kyc_note: Beneficial ownership on file; counterparty list NOT on file — the institution does not collect expected-counterparty data for this segment.

activity: Incoming payments from a freight forwarder; outgoing wires to component brokers in two transshipment hubs.
Trade documents reference HS codes matching export-controlled microelectronics.
The company has NO trade history before incorporation; director previously at a deregistered trading firm.
P-NV-ec.customer: Business account — electronics wholesaler incorporated 8 months ago. SYNTHETIC.
P-NV-ec.kyc_note: Trade-document screening is out of scope for every legacy TM rule; the institution holds the docs in a separate trade-finance system.

activity: Sudden daily debit-card cash withdrawals at the branch ATM ($400–800), prior pattern was one monthly visit.
New e-transfer payees added in a two-week burst; amounts drain the savings sweep.
Branch note: customer accompanied by an unfamiliar 'helper' on two visits; a power-of-attorney change is in progress.
P-NV-efe.customer: Personal account, 23-year tenure, customer age 81. SYNTHETIC.
P-NV-efe.kyc_note: File notes a documented cognitive-impairment accommodation from 2024. No legacy TM rule covers elder financial exploitation.

activity: Online-banking logins routed through VPN exit nodes; two sessions geolocate to a comprehensively sanctioned jurisdiction.
Card purchases at a virtual-asset platform within hours of those sessions.
Fiat withdrawals from the same platform land back in the account days later.
P-NV-vc.customer: Personal account, 3-year tenure, crypto-exchange on/off-ramps in profile. SYNTHETIC.
P-NV-vc.kyc_note: Login telemetry sits in the fraud stack, not the AML stack — the legacy rulebook has no access-geography rule.

activity: Cash deposits spike every February and May (holiday trade), 160% of monthly average.
Supplier payments to two wholesale nurseries; payroll for three staff.
Pattern repeats across all 12 years of history.
P-RP-01.kyc_note: Declared seasonal cash business at onboarding; expected-volume field anticipates the seasonal peaks.

activity: Biweekly salary credit, monthly mortgage debit, automatic savings sweep.
One out-of-pattern event: a $30,000 incoming transfer with memo 'estate distribution', matched by a probate-note on file.
P-RP-02.kyc_note: KYC current; the estate transfer is documented in a branch note from the same week.

activity: Lumpy invoice income: $4,000–11,000 credits at irregular intervals from 5 repeat counterparties.
Three round-amount transfers of $2,000 to the same family member in 60 days (below TM-105's five-transfer trigger).
Periodic cash withdrawals for materials purchases (declared trade: renovation contractor).
P-RP-03.customer: Personal account — independent contractor, 6-year tenure. SYNTHETIC.
P-RP-03.kyc_note: Occupation documented; counterparties consistent with the declared trade.

TM-101.indicator: A customer makes multiple cash deposits just below the currency transaction reporting threshold within a short period, in a pattern consistent with structuring to avoid the filing requirement.
TM-101.logic: three or more cash deposits each between $8,000 and $9,999 into one account within any rolling 7-day window.

signal.red_flag: Structuring — repeated sub-threshold cash deposits to evade CTR filing

TM-101.title: Structuring below the reporting threshold

TM-102.indicator: Funds are deposited and then promptly withdrawn or transferred out within one to two business days, leaving a minimal balance and showing no apparent business or personal purpose for the pass-through activity.
TM-102.logic: incoming credits ≥ $20,000 followed by outgoing debits of 90% or more of the credited amount within 48 hours, twice in 30 days.

signal.red_flag: Rapid in-and-out movement with no economic purpose (pass-through account)

TM-102.title: Rapid movement of funds

TM-104.indicator: A customer sends or receives international wire transfers involving high-risk jurisdictions with no documented economic purpose or relationship to the destination country.
TM-104.logic: any wire ≥ $10,000 to or from a jurisdiction on the institution's high-risk country list where the customer profile records no business or family connection to that jurisdiction.

signal.red_flag: Unexplained wires to/from high-risk jurisdictions with no customer nexus

TM-104.title: Unexplained high-risk geography wires

TM-106.indicator: A business customer's cash deposit volume substantially and persistently exceeds the expected activity stated in its onboarding profile, without a corresponding change in the declared nature of the business.
TM-106.logic: monthly cash deposits exceeding 200% of the declared expected cash volume recorded at onboarding, for two consecutive months.

signal.red_flag: Cash deposits far exceeding the declared business cash profile

TM-106.title: Cash activity inconsistent with business profile

TM-108.indicator: An account exhibits a sudden spike in transaction frequency relative to its own historical baseline that is not explained by seasonality or a documented life event.
TM-108.logic: transaction count in any 7-day window exceeding six times the trailing 90-day weekly average, minimum 25 transactions.

signal.red_flag: Sudden transaction-velocity spike vs the account's own baseline

TM-108.title: Transaction velocity spike

TM-109.indicator: An account receives cash deposits in multiple geographically dispersed locations followed by prompt consolidated withdrawal or onward transfer elsewhere, consistent with funnel account activity used to move illicit proceeds across regions.
TM-109.logic: cash deposits into one account at branches in three or more distinct cities within 14 days, followed by consolidation and withdrawal or transfer in a different region.

signal.red_flag: Funnel account — dispersed multi-city cash-in, consolidated withdrawal elsewhere

TM-109.title: Funnel account pattern

TM-110.indicator: Incoming wire transfers repeatedly arrive with missing or incomplete originator information, suggesting deliberate stripping of payment details to obscure the source of funds.
TM-110.logic: two or more incoming wires within 90 days where originator name, address, or account fields are missing, truncated, or populated with filler characters.

signal.red_flag: Incoming wires with stripped or incomplete originator information

TM-110.title: Incomplete originator information on incoming wires

TM-112.indicator: A customer splits international remittances into multiple below-threshold transactions routed through different money services businesses to the same destination, consistent with deliberate fragmentation to avoid scrutiny.
TM-112.logic: outgoing remittances from one customer through two or more money services business counterparties to the same beneficiary country, each below $3,000, aggregate ≥ $9,000 in 30 days.

signal.red_flag: Remittances fragmented across MSBs below thresholds to one destination

TM-112.title: Split international remittances across MSBs
